newsitem.title: INDIA: India police search for missing "Bandit Queen".
newsitem.headline: India police search for missing "Bandit Queen".

text.p: Indian police issued a nationwide alert for the arrest of former "Bandit Queen" Phoolan Devi on Tuesday after the member of parliament, wanted in dozens of cases including murder, failed to appear in court.
Devi ignored a summons to appear in court on Tuesday in the northern industrial town of Kanpur, where she faced arrest warrants in 57 pending cases.
Police said they were unable to track her down despite raids on two of her residences.
"We raided her residences in Delhi but could not find her anywhere," police officer Shyam Pal Singh told the Kanpur court, which was ringed by police.
Crowds of people, kept away from the court by the tight security, packed balconies and terraces of nearby buildings.

Singh said police had spent five days searching for Devi in Delhi, raiding two homes and looking for her in a state hospital and the Supreme Court, where she had been expected to appear recently for an unsuccessful appeal against the warrants.
"We have sent messages to all district superintendents of police throughout the country to arrest Phoolan Devi wherever she is sighted," Kanpur police chief Rajiv Ranjan Verma said.

Movie maker Sekhar Kapoor portrayed Devi, who belongs to the low-caste Mallah community of boatmen, as a low-caste heroine in the biographical film "Bandit Queen" which won praise at several international film festivals.
In New Delhi, police used water cannon to disperse several hundred of Devi's supporters who tried to break through a barricade during a protest against efforts to arrest her.
"She is completely shattered," Phoolan Devi's husband, Umedh Singh, said. "... we have launched this agitation throughout the country and we will not allow her to be arrested."
Devi shot to notoriety after 22 upper-caste men were killed in a massacre at Behmai village, near Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh state in 1981.
She was accused of leading a gang in the massacre but denied the charges. Devi surrendered to the police in 1983 under an amnesty offered by the central state of Madhya Pradesh.
She spent more than 10 years in prison before being released on parole in 1994.

The chief minister of Uttar Pradesh state then withdrew all cases against her and inducted her into his Samajwadi Party, a regional Socialist party which represents low castes. She easily won a constituency in elections last May.
The state's high court revived the cases after a man who claimed to be one of her intended victims asked that they be reinstated.
Judge S.K. Srivastava rejected a demand by Devi's lawyer to withdraw the arrest warrants, and ordered police to produce Devi in court on February 17.
